basic_identification.name: NEW INC (New Museum)
basic_identification.originator: Lisa Phillips (New Museum Director), Karen Wong (Deputy Director/Co-Founder of NEW INC); New Museum of Contemporary Art
basic_identification.geography: New York City, USA; operates from the New Museum building on the Bowery, Lower East Side

core_ideas.core_claim: NEW INC is the first museum-led cultural incubator, founded on the premise that artists and creative practitioners need entrepreneurial infrastructure — studio space, mentorship, peer community, and business development — to build sustainable practices at the intersection of art, design, and technology. It positions the museum not just as an exhibiting institution but as an active producer of cultural entrepreneurship.
core_ideas.medium_specificity: Digitally native in orientation: the incubator is organized around tracks that foreground technology-driven practice, including Art & Code, Creative Science, and Spatial Design. Members work with VR/AR, machine learning, creative coding, blockchain, interactive media, and other digital-native tools. The incubator specifically selects for practitioners whose work would not exist without digital infrastructure, though it does not exclude physical or hybrid practices.
core_ideas.relation_to_attention_economy: NEW INC operates partially within attention logic through its Demo Day events and public showcases, which function as visibility-generating spectacles for members. The annual cohort cycle creates periodic attention spikes. However, the core value proposition is structural — providing workspace, mentorship, and community — rather than engagement-driven. The incubator does not optimize for algorithmic attention but benefits from the New Museum's institutional visibility and media presence. Members' individual practices may be attention-dependent (social media, platform presence) but the incubator itself prioritizes sustained development over viral moments.
core_ideas.relation_to_intention: Strongly intention-aligned. NEW INC serves a declared structural need in the field: sustainable livelihoods for art-technology practitioners. The incubator model explicitly addresses the gap between artistic practice and economic viability. It provides infrastructure (space, mentorship, community) rather than capturing engagement. However, the startup/entrepreneurship framing can introduce venture-capital-adjacent logic that privileges scalability and market fit over artistic integrity.

market_economics.revenue_model: Membership fees from annual cohort members (approximately $600/month for studio membership as of recent cohorts). Additional revenue from New Museum institutional support, foundation grants (Ford Foundation, Knight Foundation, among others), corporate partnerships, and event sponsorships. The incubator is subsidized by the New Museum and is not designed to be independently profitable.
market_economics.market_position: Infrastructure and capacity building. Not a marketplace but an enabler of market-ready practices. Sits upstream of primary market activity — helps practitioners develop businesses, products, and artistic careers that then enter various markets.
market_economics.price_range: Not directly applicable as a sales platform. Member projects range from free open-source tools to venture-backed startups to gallery-priced artworks. The diversity of outputs means no single price range applies.
market_economics.volume_trend_2024_2026: Stable. NEW INC has maintained consistent annual cohorts of approximately 60-100 members since its founding. The incubator model has proven resilient through the NFT boom and bust, as its value proposition is not tied to speculative markets. Post-pandemic, the program has adapted to hybrid formats. [uncertain]
market_economics.collector_demographics: Not directly applicable. NEW INC members' work reaches diverse audiences depending on their practice: some enter the traditional art market (galleries, collectors), others build tech products (users, investors), and others produce public or community-oriented work. The incubator itself does not have collectors. [uncertain]
market_economics.sustainability: Moderately sustainable. The model depends on continued New Museum institutional support and external grant funding. Membership fees cover a portion of operating costs but likely not the full program. The incubator is not self-sustaining without institutional subsidy. However, the New Museum's commitment to the program has been consistent for over a decade, and the model has been emulated by other institutions, suggesting it fills a genuine structural need. Risk: dependent on the New Museum's financial health and strategic priorities.

practice_aesthetics.toolchain: Highly diverse across cohort members: creative coding frameworks (p5.js, Processing, openFrameworks, TouchDesigner), machine learning tools (TensorFlow, PyTorch, RunwayML), blockchain/smart contract platforms, VR/AR development (Unity, Unreal Engine), web technologies, hardware prototyping (Arduino, Raspberry Pi), and various proprietary and open-source creative tools. No single toolchain — reflects the diversity of art-technology practice.
practice_aesthetics.relation_to_AI: AI is increasingly central. Recent cohorts include practitioners working with generative AI as a medium, building AI-powered creative tools, and critically examining AI's cultural implications. NEW INC has hosted workshops and discussions on AI ethics, creative AI, and the impact of large language models on creative practice. AI is engaged with as tool, medium, subject, and industry disruptor simultaneously.
practice_aesthetics.liveness: Full spectrum across members: static artifacts, interactive installations, real-time performances, generative systems, software products, and evolving platforms. The incubator does not prescribe a single mode of practice.
practice_aesthetics.aesthetic_vocabulary: Borrows from multiple vocabularies: startup/entrepreneurship language (MVP, pitch, product-market fit), contemporary art discourse (conceptual frameworks, critical theory), design thinking (user experience, prototyping), and technology culture (open source, hacking, making). This hybrid vocabulary is both a strength (bridging communities) and a weakness (sometimes reducing art to product logic or vice versa). The critical vocabulary specific to art-technology incubation is still forming.
practice_aesthetics.tendency_axis_position: Openness tilting toward enclosure: members share knowledge within the cohort but develop proprietary products/businesses. Commons tilting toward capture: community-building ethos alongside startup logic that drives toward private value creation. Infrastructure over spectacle: the core offering is workspace and mentorship, though Demo Days create spectacle moments. Individual tilting from collective: supports individual practices within a cohort community structure.

infrastructure_governance.openness: Hybrid. The incubator model itself is not open-source, though it has been documented and emulated. Individual member projects range from fully open-source to proprietary. NEW INC does not impose licensing requirements on member work. Internal knowledge sharing happens within the cohort but is not systematically published. Some programming and events are open to the public.
infrastructure_governance.governance_model: Institutional/curatorial. The New Museum leadership (Karen Wong as key figure) sets strategic direction. A selection committee determines annual cohort membership. Track leads provide mentorship within specific domains. Members have community voice but not formal governance power. Decision-making is top-down within a supportive institutional framework.
infrastructure_governance.data_sovereignty: Members retain full ownership of their work, IP, and data. NEW INC does not take equity stakes in member projects (unlike many tech incubators). This is a significant and deliberate distinction from the tech accelerator model. Members can leave with everything they built.
infrastructure_governance.interoperability: Low. NEW INC is a physical/community infrastructure, not a technical platform. No APIs, data standards, or machine-readable outputs. The alumni network creates informal interoperability through personal connections. No systematic way to connect NEW INC's knowledge base to other systems.
infrastructure_governance.preservation_strategy: Minimal formal preservation. The New Museum's archive may document NEW INC programming, but there is no dedicated preservation strategy for member projects. Individual members are responsible for preserving their own work. The ephemeral nature of much art-technology practice means significant work may be lost. [uncertain]
infrastructure_governance.consent_architecture: Standard institutional consent through membership agreements. Members consent to participation terms, promotional use of their work, and community norms. No granular or machine-readable consent architecture. Consent is binary (join or don't join) with standard contractual terms.

field_position.relation_to_traditional_art_world: Integration through the New Museum connection. NEW INC benefits from museum legitimacy while operating outside traditional exhibition/collection logic. Members gain access to art world networks, curators, and critics through the New Museum association. However, the incubator's entrepreneurship framing can create tension with traditional art world values. Some alumni have gone on to significant gallery and museum careers; others have built tech companies that operate entirely outside the art world.
field_position.what_it_enables: Sustainable livelihoods for art-technology practitioners who fall between traditional art world support structures and tech industry frameworks. A peer community that reduces isolation. Access to mentorship from both art and business worlds. Institutional legitimacy for experimental practice. A proving ground for art-technology business models. A bridge between museum culture and creative entrepreneurship.
field_position.what_it_lacks: Long-term support beyond the annual cohort cycle — alumni receive some continued access but the intensive support ends. Geographic limitation to NYC (though some programming has gone virtual). A mechanism for supporting practitioners who cannot afford membership fees. Critical discourse infrastructure — the incubator prioritizes making over theorizing. A way to measure or communicate impact beyond individual success stories. International reach beyond the NYC art-tech ecosystem.
field_position.who_is_excluded: Practitioners who cannot afford NYC living costs plus membership fees. Artists whose work does not fit entrepreneurship/business development framing. Non-English speakers face practical barriers. Practitioners outside NYC who cannot attend in-person programming. Those without prior institutional connections may not know about or feel eligible for the program. The application process inherently selects for those comfortable with startup-adjacent language and self-presentation.
field_position.frontier_signal: Established. NEW INC was frontier when launched in 2014 as the first museum-led incubator. The model is now established and has been replicated. The institution remains relevant but is no longer the novel experiment it once was. Current frontier questions: how to evolve beyond the annual cohort model, how to address equity and access, how to remain relevant as AI transforms creative practice.

attention_intention.discovery_mechanism: Institutional reputation (New Museum brand), word of mouth within NYC art-tech community, social media presence, annual open call for applications, alumni network referrals, arts and technology media coverage, partnerships with other organizations.
attention_intention.attention_dependency: Low-moderate. The incubator's core value is physical/community infrastructure, not online attention. It would survive the disappearance of social media platforms. However, member recruitment and public visibility benefit from social media and media coverage. The New Museum's institutional reputation provides attention independent of platforms.
attention_intention.intention_alignment: Intention-native. The incubator serves a declared structural need (sustainable creative practice) through infrastructure (space, mentorship, community). The entrepreneurship framing introduces some market-capture logic, but the overall orientation is toward enabling practitioners rather than extracting engagement. The no-equity-stake policy is a clear intention-aligned design choice.
attention_intention.commons_contribution: Moderate. NEW INC contributes to commons through public events, shared knowledge within cohorts, and the demonstration effect of its model (inspiring similar programs). However, much of the value created is private (member businesses, proprietary projects). The alumni network is a semi-commons resource. The incubator does not systematically produce open knowledge, data, or infrastructure for the broader field.

provenance_temporality.provenance_type: Neither ownership nor meaning provenance in the A(DAI) sense. The incubator tracks membership (who was in which cohort) but does not provide provenance for artworks or ideas. Individual member projects may implement their own provenance systems.
provenance_temporality.temporal_logic: Cyclical (annual cohort cycle) with some archival quality (alumni records, documentation of past cohorts). Not anticipatory or deep-historical in a systematic way. The annual cycle creates a rhythm of application, incubation, showcase, and graduation.
provenance_temporality.absence_handling: Limited systematic absence detection. The selection process implicitly identifies what is missing (seeking diversity in each cohort), but there is no formal mechanism for mapping gaps in the field. The incubator responds to emerging practices (adding AI-focused members, for example) but reactively rather than through systematic field sensing.

coherence.coherence_vs_consensus: Coherence. Each cohort brings together diverse practices — artists, designers, technologists, researchers — that coexist without requiring agreement on method or values. The incubator holds together art-world and startup-world logics that would normally be in tension. Coherence is maintained through shared physical space and community norms rather than ideological alignment.
coherence.contestability: Low. Cohort selection decisions are not contestable. The incubator's direction is set by institutional leadership. Members can voice concerns within the community but have no formal governance mechanism. The main form of contestability is exit — choosing not to apply or not to renew.
coherence.forkability: High for the model, low for the institution. The incubator model has already been forked/adapted by other institutions (Eyebeam, Gray Area, various museum programs). The specific community, New Museum brand, and NYC location are not forkable. The concept is highly portable.

adai_comparison.what_adai_should_adopt: The no-equity-stake principle — supporting practitioners without extracting ownership of their work. The cohort model as a way to build peer community. The hybrid vocabulary that bridges art and technology worlds without collapsing either. The physical/community infrastructure approach that creates real relationships, not just data connections. The demonstration that museums can actively support creative production, not just exhibition.
adai_comparison.what_adai_should_refuse: The startup/entrepreneurship framing that reduces art to product logic. The geographic concentration in a single expensive city. The membership fee model that creates economic barriers to participation. The annual cohort cycle that provides intensive but time-limited support. The lack of systematic knowledge production or commons contribution. The absence of critical discourse infrastructure alongside the making infrastructure.
adai_comparison.structural_tension: NEW INC demonstrates that museum-adjacent infrastructure can support art-technology practice, but it does so through an entrepreneurship lens that A(DAI) would find insufficient. The productive tension is between NEW INC's pragmatic support for individual practitioners and A(DAI)'s ambition to build collective intelligence infrastructure for the entire field. NEW INC asks 'how can artists sustain their practice?' while A(DAI) asks 'how can the field sustain its own knowledge?' Both questions matter but they pull in different directions — individual sustainability versus collective infrastructure.

regulatory_legal.regulatory_exposure: Operates under US nonprofit law (through the New Museum's 501(c)(3) status). Standard employment and contractor regulations apply to staff. Members are independent operators responsible for their own regulatory compliance. No direct exposure to EU AI Act or crypto-specific regulation, though individual member projects may be affected. The incubator itself is regulatory-light.
regulatory_legal.ip_model: Members retain all IP. NEW INC does not take equity or IP stakes. This is a deliberate policy distinction from tech accelerators. Individual members choose their own IP strategies (patents, copyrights, open-source licenses, CC licenses, etc.). The incubator imposes no IP requirements.
regulatory_legal.opt_in_vs_opt_out: Opt-in. Participation is entirely voluntary through an annual application process. No default inclusion. Members actively choose to apply, pay fees, and participate.

ecosystem.platform_dependency: Low. The incubator depends on physical space (New Museum building) and institutional support (New Museum organization) but not on any digital platform. If any social media platform disappeared, the core program would be unaffected. Dependency is institutional rather than platform-based.
ecosystem.network_effects: Moderate hub. NEW INC functions as a connector between art-world and tech-world networks in NYC. The alumni network creates compounding value over time as past members achieve visibility and can mentor/support new members. However, the network effects are geographically concentrated and not systematically leveraged.
ecosystem.post_crash_trajectory: Stable. The incubator was not dependent on NFT markets and was not significantly affected by the 2022-2023 crypto crash. Some cohort members working in crypto/NFT spaces may have been individually affected, but the program itself continued without disruption. The incubator's value proposition (workspace, community, mentorship) is market-cycle-independent. [uncertain]
